task_description: Write a method in Dafny to convert an array to a sequence.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method ArrayToSequence(a: array<int>) returns (seqResult: seq<int>)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The returned sequence seqResult is equal to the sequence of elements in the input array a in order
- The length of seqResult is equal to the length of the array a
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method ArrayToSequence(a: array<int>) returns (seqResult: seq<int>)
    
Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - There are no preconditions, the method will always work. Arrays can be empty or non-empty.
    
Dafny specification:
    requires a != null;
    
Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The resulting sequence contains all elements of the input array in the same order
    
Dafny specification:
    ensures seqResult == a[..]
    
Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method ArrayToSequence(a: array<int>) returns (seqResult: seq<int>)
    requires a != null
    ensures seqResult == a[..]
{
    var s: seq<int> := "";
    var i := 0;
    while i < a.Length
        invariant 0 <= i <= a.Length
        invariant s == a[..i]
    {
        s := s + a[i];
        i := i + 1;
    }
    seqResult := s;
}
```
